name: Arc I Finale: The Errand of the Vessel

text.content:
Levels 4–5. The climax of Arc I, running through the nine days before the Night of the Eye and resolving on it. Renamed from "The Black Master's Errand" to avoid confusion with [[arc-two]], which is a different mission entirely.

DM Note — Why This Arc Matters More Than It Looks

Ossian Krell carried the draconian corruption ritual out of Sanction by scarifying it into his own body over eleven months, in eleven incomplete overlapping passes, so it could not be confiscated or copied. He is the document. Destroying the knowledge means killing him; preserving it means keeping a living man in a vault forever.

On the Night of the Eye, Raistlin proposes a fourth option: draw the working out of the living man and into a vessel that cannot run, cannot bargain and cannot die. It will work. It will also empty the man it is drawn out of.

This is the Long Return in miniature, three arcs early. The party watches Raistlin move a thing written into a person out of that person and into a container, on the grounds that it is the least-worst option available — and he is right.

When he does it again in Arc V, to his brother, at least one player will remember this night. Play the parallel straight and never point at it.

The vessel goes into the Wayreth vaults. If you are running the full campaign, it is still there in Arc V, and someone may think to ask what became of Krell.

The Errand of the Black Master now begins as a road campaign: Ispin's funeral, the first appearance of the Dragon Queen's forces, and a thirty-nine-day race from Vogler to Wayreth before the Night of the Eye.

Part One: The Road to Wayreth

Begin on 18 Darkember. Preserve the published funeral and the party's first experience of the Dragonarmy. Once they have witnessed draconians and reached a moment of safety, Ispin's black invitation awakens and names 1 Newkolt as the Night of the Eye. The party chooses one of three physical routes south; the Forest will not simply open beside Vogler.

The Present Crisis

Ossian Krell, former apprentice to the Dragonarmy mage Dracart, has fled with the method by which good dragon eggs are corrupted into draconians. The ritual cannot be carried in an ordinary book. It is written into his own living skin and memory. Raistlin knows Krell is moving south and has arranged for Ispin's chosen witnesses to collide with him on the road.

PartLocationPurpose
PrologueVoglerIspin's funeral, first Dragonarmy violence, invitation awakens.
Road ArcOne of three routes across Solamnia/Lemish/New Sea8–16 sessions of travel, war, Krell, pursuit, and accumulated knowledge.
Act IIForest of WayrethThe Forest admits the party and refuses Krell.
Act IIIWayrethNine days of investigation, politics, courtship, and an optional Test.
Act IVNight of the EyeThe final choice over Krell and the ritual.

Use The Road to Wayreth: Thirty-Nine Days as the master travel journal and the selected route journal for the full pre-Wayreth arc.

Run this during the funeral gathering in Vogler after every character has had time to remember Ispin and before the campaign's first Dragonarmy alarms become the only thing anyone can think about.

Becklin's Packet

Becklin asks the party to remain when the other mourners leave the table. Ispin left a leather map case for the friends who came when called. Inside are his map of central Ansalon, three route strips, his green wax seal, and the black invitation bearing every character's name.

His note to Becklin remains characteristically direct: If they ask whether the mage is dangerous, tell them yes. If they ask whether that means they should refuse, tell them they have learned nothing from me.

Memories That Matter

Ask each player one question and record the answer. Wayreth will use those memories later.

  • When did Ispin trust you with something more valuable than money?
  • What story did he tell that you never believed?
  • What promise did he extract from you as a joke?
  • What did he know about you that you hoped he had forgotten?
  • Why would he think you could stand before a room of wizards and remain yourself?

Do Not Activate It Yet

The invitation remains dormant through the funeral and the first battle. Let the party witness what the Dragon Queen has brought to Vogler before the wizard plot moves. The road matters because it begins after something real has been lost.

DM Note — Why Ispin Knew Wayreth

Years ago Ispin carried an injured apprentice out of a ruin rather than taking the spellbook they both came to recover. The apprentice was Antimodes, who later told Par-Salian and eventually Raistlin. Ispin never entered Wayreth. He earned the rarer distinction of being discussed there favorably.

Wait until the party is safe enough after the first Dragonarmy violence for silence to return. Then the black card becomes cold.

The Silver Writing

You have seen what the Queen is making.

On the first day of Newkolt the three moons will stand together. Be at Wayreth before they do.

Ossian Krell carries the method of their making south. Bring him if you judge him worth bringing. Bring only the truth if you judge otherwise.

The forest will not come to you.

— R.M.

Ispin's Map

The marked map now resolves into three clear corridors: the Sailor’s Road through Kalaman, Mirivale, Hylo, and Gilthanost; the River and Heartland Road through the Dargaard corridor, Maelgoth, Brasdel, Solanthus, and Garnet before a Gilthanost or Zaradene branch; and the Wild Road through Cericas, Fangoth, Solace, Haven, and Pax Tharkas. Competent travelers can estimate that all three require roughly a month. The calendar gives them thirty-nine days, but anyone knowledgeable about Wayreth warns that arriving on the day of the conjunction is arriving too late.

The Clock

Put 39 days remain in front of the players. Advance the module calendar openly. Long rests already exist inside the travel schedule; only deliberate waiting and actual delays remove whole days.

If They Refuse the Journey

Krell still crosses their path and the war still widens. Refusing is a campaign choice, not a failure state. The Night of the Eye occurs without them and Wayreth later sends a record of what the Conclave decided in their absence.

pages.name: Act I: The Defector on the Road

text.content:
Krell enters through the route the party actually chose. The characters, Krell, Skaith, and Mereth are all moving toward the same southern objective, but the road determines how their stories collide.

Place Krell by Route

RouteKrell's entry
Sailor’s RoadHidden aboard the Kalaman vessel or transferred at Mirivale under dead or forged crew papers.
River and Heartland RoadUnder guard or concealed among displaced travelers near Maelgoth and Brasdel, just before a formal road inspection exposes him.
Wild RoadIn custody at Fangoth, accused of espionage, forbidden sorcery, or entering under a false identity.

Once the party takes responsibility for him, he tells most of the truth: he was Dracart's apprentice, watched the corruption performed repeatedly, and is trying to deliver the method to the only institution he believes can contain it. He still says the ritual is “somewhere safe.” A DC 16 Insight check reveals that the answer terrifies him.

The Pursuit

Skaith, a sivak draconian officer, wants Krell recovered and uses his ability to assume appearances to make eyewitness evidence unreliable. Mereth Sorn, a renegade Black Robe in Dragonarmy service, wants Krell dead and will make the moral case for that choice before resorting to violence.

Required Road Beats

  1. The Second Krell. Skaith uses Krell's appearance while the real man is elsewhere.
  2. The Offer. Mereth argues honestly that the Conclave will preserve knowledge that should not exist.
  3. The Fever. Krell collapses and the party discovers deliberate arcane scarification across his back.

By the time the party reaches the border of Wayreth they must know that the ritual is on him, that both pursuers have defensible motives from their own perspective, and that getting Krell to the Tower is not the same thing as saving him.

The party reaches the treeline. The forest opens for them.

It does not open for Krell.

Running the Refusal

Play it four times, and make each attempt worse.

  1. He falls behind. The party walks; Krell walks; twenty minutes later he is not with them. They backtrack and find him standing at the treeline having never entered, insisting he followed them the whole way.
  2. Roped together. Someone has the obvious idea. The rope goes slack. The end of it is neatly severed and the cut is not a cut — the fibres simply stop.
  3. Carried. A PC picks him up and walks. It works for four hundred yards. Then the PC is walking alone, and behind them, at conversational distance, someone is laughing quietly. It is not Krell.
  4. Magical transit. Any attempt to teleport, dimension door, or otherwise force him inside triggers the psychic backlash from The Refused — 4d6 psychic to the caster, and the certainty of having been noticed.

Between attempts, Krell deteriorates. He has been running for four months and the forest is the last door and it will not open, and by the fourth attempt he is begging.

The Way In

There is one, and the party has to find it.

The forest is refusing the ritual, not the man. It cannot separate them, and neither can anyone else, but it can be persuaded that the party is bringing it in to be dealt with rather than to be delivered.

What works, in rough order of how satisfying it is at the table:

  • A PC states aloud, in the forest, what they intend to do with Krell once inside — and means it. No check. The forest is not measuring eloquence.
  • A PC who has passed the Test invokes the Conclave's writ. The forest admits them on Conclave business and it will hold them to it.
  • Krell himself asks to be taken in as a prisoner rather than a petitioner. This is the version the forest was waiting for, and it is the one he resists longest.

Whichever they choose, the path opens immediately, without ceremony, and it is noticeably shorter than the one they walked in on.

DM Note

This act is where an attentive party works out that the forest is making decisions the Conclave is not making. Let them. It sets up the reveal in The Black Master of Wayreth perfectly, and it means that when Par-Salian later claims the Tower admitted Krell on the Conclave's authority, at least one player at the table knows he is lying.

The Conclave convenes on the day the party arrives. It sits for nine days, as it has for every question of consequence in three hundred years, and the party spends those nine days being courted.

What They Learn on Day One

The Tower's examiners take Krell apart, professionally and without cruelty, and report what the party already suspects. The ritual is complete, it is accurate, and it is in him — layered into the dermis in eleven overlapping passes, each incomplete, each meaningless without the others.

It cannot be copied. The examiners have tried. It cannot be transcribed, imaged, or scried — Krell built that in deliberately, so that his only value was his continued existence.

He was very clever. It has worked exactly as designed and it has ruined him.

The Three Positions

WhoWantsArgument
Par-SalianKrell dead, quietly, tonightThe knowledge cannot be permitted to exist. He is not pretending it is anything other than an execution, and he is not enjoying it.
LadonnaKrell alive, in the vault, indefinitelyThe ritual is the only thing on Ansalon that explains how the corruption works, and you cannot undo a working you do not understand. She wants to save the eggs. This is true, and it is not her only reason.
JustariusKrell freed, under watchThe Orders do not imprison people for what is written on them. The moment they do, the Conclave has become the Kingpriest, and he says so in open session.

Raistlin does not state a position. For nine days he sits on the dais, listens, asks two questions, and says nothing else. Both questions should be asked of the party, in front of the Conclave, without warning.

The first, on day three: “Why did you bring him here?”

The second, on day eight: “What did you promise him?”

The Nine Days at the Table

This act is conversations, and it should be structured like a heist without a heist. Give the party the run of the public Tower and let each faction approach them:

  • Par-Salian asks them to confirm, formally, that Krell arrived as a prisoner. It is a small lie or a small truth depending on Act II, and their answer decides whether he can act without a Conclave vote.
  • Ladonna offers them the vaults. Genuinely — an item each, no conditions stated. She wants them to speak for detention when asked.
  • Justarius asks them for nothing and tells them everything, including the contents of the Sealed Library, which is a criminal act on his part and is the most useful thing anyone does for them.
  • Dalamar (if used) approaches whichever PC is least suspicious of him and asks, apparently idly, whether the forest admitted Krell or the Conclave did. He is checking something.
  • Krell asks to see the party. He is in a comfortable room with no lock, and he wants to know what they think should happen to him, and he will accept their answer.

Run the Test here if a PC is taking it.

Act III works best when each day offers evidence, an advocate, and one change in Krell. The party should have enough information to disagree intelligently by the final vote.

DayEvidenceApproachKrell
1The markings are complete and cannot be copied by ordinary means.Par-Salian asks how the forest admitted him.Relieved to be alive; asks for sleep.
2One layer describes corruption; another appears to describe reversal.Ladonna offers access to the vault catalogue.Insists there is no reversal layer.
3Krell added anti-scrying structures to make his body indispensable.Raistlin asks why the party brought him.Admits he engineered his own value.
4Several symbols match formulae recovered from Istar.Justarius reveals the legal precedent for living magical evidence.Requests counsel and is denied by a 12–9 vote.
5A damaged good dragon egg reacts to the reversal layer.Jaclyn asks the party to witness an experiment.Tries to bargain for release.
6Removing any layer conventionally would kill him.Mereth or a Dragonarmy agent breaches the forest through a stolen memory.Saves an apprentice during the breach.
7The ritual has begun adapting to Krell's healing body.Each faction makes its clearest offer.Asks what Ispin would have chosen.
8Raistlin has calculated a fourth option under the coming alignment.Raistlin asks what the party promised.Requests the truth, not comfort.
9The vessel for removal is missing from the declared inventory.The Conclave prepares to vote.Chooses what he will say if permitted.

Three Investigations

  • The body: Medicine and Arcana establish that Krell is both victim and author. Success reveals facts, never an easy cure.
  • The law: History, Persuasion, and library access uncover precedents. Every precedent solved a crisis and created a shame.
  • The Master: Insight cannot read Raistlin's motive. Following inventories, witnesses, and room access can. Let evidence answer what a single check cannot.

Pressure Without Railroading

If the party decides early, do not invalidate the decision. Let later evidence test the reason for it. A group committed to release must confront the adaptive ritual. A group committed to execution must see the damaged egg respond. A group favoring detention must meet the person who would become Krell's permanent keeper.

pages.name: War at the Edge of the Forest

text.content:
Use this optional action chapter on day six if the Tower arc needs physical danger or if the Dragonarmy should remain present during a political story.

The Breach

Skaith cannot force an army through Wayreth. Instead, he carries a memory taken from Krell: the sincere belief that the ritual belongs inside the Tower. The forest reads intention, and for several minutes Skaith's stolen conviction is more authentic than his orders. He enters with six baaz draconians and Mereth Sorn, who intends to kill Krell before either side can preserve him.

Encounter Sequence

  1. Silver warning. Doors close and moon lamps turn white. The party has three rounds to choose where to go: Krell's room, the guest range, or the Hall of Doors.
  2. Divided corridors. Run two encounters simultaneously in adjacent spaces. Each round a character may spend an action solving a tower ward to open support between them.
  3. The stolen memory. Skaith appears as Ispin Greenshield when confronting the party. The form is imperfect only in what it says: it knows facts, not affection.
  4. Mereth's choice. When she reaches Krell, he is shielding an apprentice. Mereth hesitates for one round. A character can use that round to fight, persuade, or force her to see the contradiction in her mercy.

Suggested Forces

For characters of levels 5–6, use one sivak draconian with reduced hit points, four baaz draconians, and a mage split across two scenes. For levels 7–8, use the full sivak, six baaz, and Mereth as the module's Renegade Hunter. The Tower suppresses area spells that would kill uninvolved residents unless the caster succeeds on a DC 18 spellcasting ability check.

Consequences

Capturing Skaith proves the Dragonarmy can steal identity and memory. Killing him leaves Ispin's borrowed face on the corpse until dawn. If Mereth survives, she can testify during the final Conclave, arguing that she came to destroy the ritual and discovered the Orders had made a prison around a man. If Krell saves the apprentice, every faction must account for an act that does not erase his crimes and cannot honestly be ignored.

pages.name: Act IV: The Night of the Eye

text.content:
The Conclave's ninth day falls two days before the Night of the Eye. Raistlin adjourns without a vote and sets the decision for the Night itself, and gives no reason.

The reason is that on the Night of the Eye a ritual of a scale otherwise impossible will succeed. He has been waiting for it since the day Krell arrived, and possibly since before.

The Fourth Option

In the Hall of Mages, under three full moons, with the Conclave assembled and the party present because he sent for them, Raistlin puts a fourth proposal that no one has heard.

The ritual can be taken out of Krell. Not copied — moved, in its entirety, off a living man and into a vessel that cannot run, cannot bargain, and cannot die. It requires the Night of the Eye, the Conclave's sanction, and every wizard in the building.

It will work. He has done the arithmetic and he shows it, and Par-Salian checks it in open session and cannot find the error.

It will also destroy the man it is drawn out of. Not kill — empty. Krell will survive the night, and walk out, and be nobody, for a long time.

The Vote

Twenty-one seats. The Conclave splits, seven for detention, seven for execution, six for release, one abstention, and Raistlin as Master casts no vote at all — he has proposed, and by the Orders' own rules the proposer does not vote on his own motion.

The deciding voice is the one the Conclave grants, by ancient and rarely used procedure, to those who brought the matter before it.

That is the party.

Running the Decision

Do not rush this and do not resolve it with a roll. Four options are on the table — execution, indefinite detention, release, and the ritual — and every one of them is defensible and every one has a named cost.

Krell is in the room. He is permitted to speak and he does, once, and what he says should depend entirely on how the party treated him in Act III. If they were kind to him, he asks for the ritual and says he would rather be nobody than be the reason for it. If they were not, he asks to be let go, and he is lying.

DM Note — What Raistlin Is Doing

The vessel. Nobody asks what it is. Ask the players whether they think to, and if they do not, that is the arc's closing beat.

He is looking for anything connected to Fistandantilus's work on recovering displaced souls — keys, wards, records of the Palanthas curse's exact wording. He is trying to reach his brother. See [[campaign-bible]].

That last one is the reading that makes the whole arc land as tragedy, and it is the one I would run.

Consequences by Outcome

The party choseWhat follows
ExecutionPar-Salian does it himself and does not delegate. The ritual is gone from the world. So is any hope of undoing the corruption, and the party will meet a good dragon who learns what they chose.
DetentionKrell goes into the vault. Ladonna's research bears fruit within a year and saves a clutch of eggs. Justarius resigns his seat. The Conclave has crossed a line and everyone in the building knows the date it happened.
ReleaseKrell walks. Within three months the Dragonarmy has him back, and the corruption operation triples in output, and the party finds out from a battlefield.
The ritualKrell survives and is emptied. The knowledge sits in the vault in something that cannot bargain. The party has done the least-worst thing and it does not feel like it.

Rewards

  • XP: the arc should carry a party from 5th to 8th. Award the bulk of it for Acts II and IV rather than for combat, and say so.
  • Standing. Whatever they chose, the party are now people the Conclave has procedures for. They can petition Wayreth, and the forest will admit them.
  • One item each, from The Vaults, issued by whichever faction they sided with. Granted items are recorded. Lent items are not. This matters later.
  • A wizard PC who took the Test during Act III leaves with their robe, their Order, and their Mark.

Threads Left Running

  • Mereth Sorn, if she survived Act I, is still at large and now has a personal reason to hate the party.
  • Skaith reported everything. The Dragonarmy knows the Conclave has the ritual and knows where the Conclave is, and the forest has never been tested against an army.
  • Justarius, if he resigned, is available as a patron with nothing left to lose.
  • Whatever the vessel was, it is in the vault, and Raistlin goes down most nights.

DM Note — Tying Off

If this is the party's last visit to Wayreth, close on Raistlin's one accurate sentence — the same device as the Test. He tells them, without praise or condemnation, exactly what they did. Write it before the session.

If they are coming back, close on the forest instead. They leave; the walk out is short; and one of them looks back and the treeline is already somewhere else.
